conventions.convention: Links are nonempty finite smooth oriented links in the standard oriented three-sphere. The double cover uses the character sending every component meridian to 1 modulo two; a tubular longitude with character η uses the branch model (s,z) ↦ (s,exp(iηs)z²). The cover orientation makes the complement covering orientation-preserving.

Surgery bits increase coordinatewise, while increasing filtration degree is n−|I|. Thus polygon components preserve F_p and immediate edges lower filtration by one. In the northwest–southeast over-strand chart, 0 pairs left/right endpoints and 1 pairs top/bottom endpoints; these are A/B on the mirror.

Reduced Khovanov cohomology uses F2 coefficients and the quotient by im X_p, retaining the marked-circle label 1 with reduced quantum degree j−1. It is not defined here by retaining an extra unreduced marked factor.
Surgery slopes λ, μ+λ, μ are labelled 0, 1, ∞. The all-∞ filling restores Y. The construction asserts fixed-presentation convergence, without a filtered comparison between different presentations.

Unmarked merge is multiplication and unmarked split is comultiplication. Marked merge kills the other circle's X label; marked split creates X on the new unmarked circle. All incident edges use simultaneous compatible vertex bases.
The spectral sequence has reduced Khovanov cohomology of the mirror on E2 and hat Floer homology of Σ(L) as abutment. Endpoint invariance does not assert a diagram-independent filtered chain type.

load_bearing.statement: For an ordered framed link in a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold, under the stated countable-choice analytic package and compatible subordinate surgery choices, the mod-two polygon maps form a filtered differential on the 0/1 cube, whose total homology is hat HF of the all-∞ filling. The one-coordinate case is the surgery mapping cone; the zero-coordinate case is the original hat complex.

The double branched cover of a based planar k-component unlink is #^(k−1)(S²×S¹), its mod-two hat Floer group has rank 2^(k−1), and neighboring resolution saddle maps agree with the reduced Frobenius multiplication/comultiplication in compatible marked state bases.

For the fixed based diagram and compatible branched-cover surgery choices, the direct sum of first-page edge maps is the reduced Khovanov differential of the mirror diagram in the specified smoothing convention.

For a fixed finite regular oriented link diagram, reduction at any two points away from crossings, possibly on different components, gives isomorphic bigraded F2 cohomology groups, without a canonical-isomorphism or diagram-change assertion.

Assuming AC, the all-meridians mod-two character of every nonempty finite oriented smooth link is well-defined and surjective; its cover has a chart-independent simple branch extension, and ambient isotopy gives orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic covers.
Assume ACω. Reduced normalized Khovanov cohomology over F2 of a nonempty oriented link is independent, up to noncanonical bigraded isomorphism, of diagram and chosen component.

A filtered chain complex over a field with the stated finite increasing filtration stabilizes and abuts to homology with its image filtration; this assertion alone does not compare complexes arising from different diagrams.

Assume AC and the ACω Heegaard Floer analytic package. Every fixed finite regular based diagram of a nonempty oriented link has the stated spectral sequence from reduced mirror Khovanov cohomology on E2 to hat HF of its double branched cover, with no diagram-independent filtered quasi-isomorphism assertion.

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1 says the complement-cover identification extends smoothly because it preserves boundary monodromies. Monodromy alone supplies no smooth extension across a square branch chart: for example, a nonconformal real-linear normal germ generally has no differentiable square-root lift. The argument needs an explicit tubular normalization or compatible transported branch charts, including the claimed independence from arbitrary tubular charts in 2.1. The isotopy-invariance conclusion is standard, but this smoothness step is not justified as written.
Proof 4.1 refers to 'the extra hypothesis of step1.2', but there is no step 1.2. The conditional top-input-sum hypothesis is in step 2.1.
Proof 4.1 attributes the grading calculation to 'step1.3', which does not exist. The grading calculation is step 3.1.
Proof 1.2 refers to 'the external Floer map computation in step2.1', but step 2.1 is the local quotient-algebra calculation; the external Floer input is applied in step 4.1.

The source reference names Ozsváth–Szabó 'Remark 1.1'. In the cited math/0309170v1, the relevant discussion is subsection 1.1, 'Further remarks and speculation'; 1.1 is not a numbered Remark. Its paragraph on filtered quasi-isomorphism invariance is the appropriate locator.

The Statement omits AC although axiom_use explicitly says it assumes AC through compact-surface classification, and Proof 1.1 invokes the AC-qualified surface-classification and annulus suppliers. The public hypothesis should agree with the declared proof branch.
The Statement omits the inherited AC assumption. Its axiom_use and final proof step explicitly retain choice through the branched-cover and peripheral suppliers.

The Statement presents the Floer-group and saddle-map assertions without the ACω hypothesis retained in axiom_use and Proof 5.1. Its branched-cover supplier also assumes AC. These assumptions should be explicit at the public interface.

The Example and Given omit the AC/ACω assumptions of the spectral-sequence existence theorem and Floer rank supplier actually invoked. The finite rank-nullity deduction is sound, but the example should retain the hypotheses of those inputs.

seams_checked.note: The supplier's cyclic-cover definition is knot-specific. This batch constructs its nonempty general-link double cover independently rather than extending the knot-only supplier without justification. The meridian-kernel and filling conventions agree on knots.

The integral Frobenius algebra, signed cube and normalization are reduced modulo two faithfully. Arbitrary-link reduced move invariance uses the separately opened based-link equivalence lemma rather than treating the older knot-specialized reduced clause as a general-link theorem.

Actual inputs are the closed-manifold hat definition, operation-qualified analytic package, closed-manifold invariance and explicit torus calculation. Knot/grid-specialized data are not substituted for closed-manifold surgery theory. The batch explicitly imports the additional OS surgery and unlink-map calculations; their relevant arguments in §§4 and 6 were consulted.

The half-twist lemma uses the supplier's actual positive annular formula and checks its sign by an explicit quotient model. The trefoil calculation retains the meridian slopes and proves the lens-space identification directly; it does not infer a lens space solely from homology order or invoke a stronger Kirby-classification conclusion.
